changes: Generalized the B-7365 fix: audited all main-mutating CLI paths and found B-7365 was not the only gap — wrapped 4 previously-unlocked main-mutating paths in withReentrantMainWriteLock (commitFromDraftMetadataOnMain, commitFromDraftMetadataAndMergeMain in cli-engine.ts; story_discard reset+commit and dormant dev_merge in worktree.ts), and added packages/main/src/tasks/main-write-lock-coverage.ts — a mechanical regression guard that scans for git main-mutation primitives, asserts each enclosing path holds the lock (fail-closed: unknown cwd treated as main), and is wired into lattice validate.
usage: The guard runs automatically under `lattice validate` (chained into the npm test script). Run it directly with `node packages/main/dist/tasks/main-write-lock-coverage.js` (exit 0 = all main-mutating paths locked) or `--negative-demo` (exit 1, demonstrates it bites). A future commit/merge on main shipped without the main-write-lock turns the guard red instead of silently corrupting concurrent sessions' metadata.
expectedOutcome: Guard green on the real tree (all main-mutating paths locked), bites (exit 1) on an unlocked main mutation, runs inside lattice validate; validate ALL PASS.
actualTranscript: $ node packages/main/dist/tasks/main-write-lock-coverage.js -> 'scanned 277 source files, 17 git mutation-verb sites' / 'PASS - all 7 main-mutating path(s) hold the main write lock' (exit 0). $ ... --negative-demo -> 'core/__negative_fixture__.ts:3 [commit] mutates-main=YES locked=NO VIOLATION' / 'FAIL' (exit 1). $ lattice validate '{"storyId":"B-9177"}' -> guard marker + 'negative fixture bites' + 'PASS' + 'ALL PASS', verification 9/9 covered.
outcomeDiff: Match. Audit found 4 real gaps (B-7365 was not the last); all wrapped lock-only; guard reports 7 main-mutating paths all locked, bites on unlocked main mutation including future gitFile-based commits (F-001 fix), and runs under validate. No semantic change.
limitations: Bounded to lock-coverage hardening + the regression guard. Full per-session physical checkout isolation (Option B) is intentionally OUT OF SCOPE (deferred maximalist architecture, recorded in scope-boundary.json). The guard scans packages/main/src for known git-wrapper shapes; a brand-new git wrapper opener would need adding to GIT_CALL_OPENERS (the fail-closed default still treats unrecognized cwd as main, so it errs toward flagging, not silently passing).
pitfalls: F-001 (medium): the guard initially did not recognize the gitFile wrapper, a latent false-negative blind spot — fixed by recognizing gitFile and classifying its calls by target ref (fail-closed updatesStoryBranchRef rejects refs/heads/main). F-002 (low): a header comment over-claimed write-tree coverage — corrected. Re-review note: each finding-fix commit stales the prior round's review bindings, forcing a fresh review round (Rounds 1->2->3); this is by design (reviewers must re-verify the changed tree), so converge fixes before re-spawning reviewers. Use withReentrantMainWriteLock (not the non-reentrant variant) for any path reachable from an already-locked flow or it self-deadlocks.
